questions.title: BST Insert Keys
questions.description:
The node type is defined for you as typedef struct BNode { int key; struct BNode *left, *right; } BNode; and the harness reads a sequence of keys and inserts each one into an initially empty BST by calling your function.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    BNode *bst_insert(BNode *root, int key)

It must insert key into the search tree (smaller keys go left, larger go right) and return the (possibly new) root. If key is already present, do NOT insert a duplicate — just return the root. The harness prints the inorder traversal of the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: k. Line 2: k space-separated keys (inserted in the given order).

Output Format:
One line with the sorted inorder sequence of distinct keys, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 1000, |key| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Ticket Priority Ordering
questions.description:
A help desk feeds ticket priorities into a BST so an inorder walk lists them in processing order. Duplicate priorities are ignored (one ticket slot per priority). The node type is defined for you as typedef struct BNode { int key; struct BNode *left, *right; } BNode; and the harness inserts every read priority by calling your function.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    BNode *bst_insert(BNode *root, int key)

It must insert key into the search tree (smaller left, larger right), skip duplicates, and return the (possibly new) root. The harness prints the inorder traversal.

Input Format:
Line 1: k. Line 2: k space-separated priorities (inserted in the given order).

Output Format:
One line with the sorted distinct priorities, space-separated.

Constraints:

questions.title: Access Code Verification
questions.description:

The node type is defined for you as typedef struct BNode { int key; struct BNode *left, *right; } BNode; and the harness builds the BST (line 1: k; line 2: k codes), then reads m attempts (line 3: m; line 4: m codes), calling your function for each.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

    int bst_search(BNode *root, int key)

It must return 1 when key exists in the tree, 0 otherwise. The harness prints one result per attempt on its own line.

Output Format:
m lines, each 1 (valid) or 0 (invalid), in attempt order.

Constraints:
1 <= k, m <= 1000, |code| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Build the Min-Heap
questions.description:
A cache server converts an array of task costs into a MIN-HEAP (array form: children of i are 2*i+1 and 2*i+2, parent never larger than a child). The conversion MUST use Floyd's bottom-up heapify: for i from n/2 - 1 down to 0, sift a[i] down; on each sift step swap the node with its SMALLER child (the left child if both are equal) and continue sifting from that slot.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void build_min_heap(int a[], int n)

It must rearrange a[0..n-1] IN PLACE into the heap produced by that exact procedure. The harness prints the resulting array space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated distinct integers.

Output Format:
One line with the heap array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, |value| <= 1000000000 (values distinct)

questions.title: Emergency Room Triage
questions.description:
An ER pushes patient severities into a MIN-HEAP as they arrive, then calls patients in severity order by repeated pop-minimum. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement these two functions:

    void heap_push(int heap[], int *size, int v)
    int heap_pop(int heap[], int *size)

heap_push must insert v at the end and sift it up while it is smaller than its parent (parent of i is (i-1)/2). heap_pop must remove and return heap[0]: move the last element to the root, shrink the size, and sift down by swapping with the smaller child until the heap property holds. The harness pushes all values, then pops until the heap is empty, printing each popped value.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated severities (arrival order).

Output Format:
One line with the pop order (ascending severities), space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, |severity| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Keys in the Range
questions.description:
A rating service keeps scores in a BST and counts how many fall inside a closed range [lo, hi]. The node type is defined for you as typedef struct BNode { int key; struct BNode *left, *right; } BNode; and the harness builds the BST from the input (line 1: k; line 2: k distinct keys; line 3: lo hi).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int bst_range_count(BNode *root, int lo, int hi)

It must return the number of keys x with lo <= x <= hi, pruning subtrees the range cannot reach (use the BST property instead of visiting everything).

Input Format:
Line 1: k. Line 2: k space-separated distinct keys. Line 3: lo and hi.

Output Format:
One line with the count.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 1000, |key| <= 1000000000, lo <= hi

Implement only this function:

    int is_min_heap(int a[], int n)

It must return 1 when a[0..n-1] is a valid min-heap, 0 otherwise. Inspect each child against its parent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Expire a BST Key
questions.description:
A session store removes an expired key from its BST, keeping the BST property: a node with two children is replaced by its INORDER SUCCESSOR (the smallest key of the right subtree); a node with one child is replaced by that child; a leaf is simply removed. The node type is defined for you as typedef struct BNode { int key; struct BNode *left, *right; } BNode; and the harness builds the BST (line 1: k; line 2: k distinct keys; line 3: the key to delete, guaranteed present).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    BNode *bst_delete(BNode *root, int key)

It must delete the node holding key (free it) and return the (possibly new) root. The harness prints the inorder traversal afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: k. Line 2: k space-separated distinct keys. Line 3: the key to delete (present).

Output Format:
One line with the remaining keys in inorder, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= k <= 1000, |key| <= 1000000000, values distinct

questions.title: Validate the BST
questions.description:
A corrupted import may have violated the BST contract, so the store re-validates: every node's key must lie strictly inside the (min, max) bounds inherited from its ancestors — left subtrees get an updated upper bound, right subtrees an updated lower bound. The node type is defined for you as typedef struct BNode { int key; struct BNode *left, *right; } BNode; and the harness builds a PLAIN binary tree from level-order input (line 1: n; line 2: n values, -1 marks a missing child), which may or may not be a BST, then calls your function with wide bounds.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_bst(BNode *root, long long lo, long long hi)

It must return 1 when every key satisfies lo < key < hi recursively (updating bounds on the way down), 0 otherwise. An empty tree is a valid BST.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated level-order values (-1 marks a missing child).

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, |value| <= 1000000000, values distinct, first value not -1

questions.title: Nearest Sensor Reading
questions.description:
A calibration probe finds the BST-stored reading CLOSEST to a target temperature (test data guarantees the closest key is unique). The node type is defined for you as typedef struct BNode { int key; struct BNode *left, *right; } BNode; and the harness builds the BST (line 1: k; line 2: k distinct keys; line 3: the target).

Implement only this function:

    int bst_closest(BNode *root, int target)

It must return the key minimizing |key - target| by walking down the tree from the root: track the best candidate seen, and descend left or right by the BST property (stop early on an exact match).

Input Format:
Line 1: k. Line 2: k space-separated distinct keys. Line 3: the target.

Output Format:
One line with the closest key.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 1000, |key|, |target| <= 1000000000 (closest key unique)
